Theorem
[An interior quasisolution is a minimizer] 1. ch11:11.11\group gt-ch11 Source: gilbarg-trudinger:page-0303, gilbarg-trudinger:page-0304 Let $u$ be a $K$-quasisolution satisfying \begin{equation} \tag {11.22} \| u\| _{C^{0,1}(\overline\Omega )}<K. \end{equation} If $F$ is jointly convex in $(z,p)$, then $u$ solves $\mathcal P$.
Proof

\sketch For $v\in \mathcal C$, condition (11.22) permits $w=(1-\varepsilon )u+\varepsilon v\in \mathcal C_K$ for small $\varepsilon >0$. Minimality on $\mathcal C_K$ and convexity give

\[ I(u)\leq I(w)\leq (1-\varepsilon )I(u)+\varepsilon I(v), \]

hence $I(u)\leq I(v)$.

□
